subject: biology
title: Codominance and multiple alleles: ABO blood groups
key_idea: The ABO blood group is controlled by one gene with three alleles: IA, IB and IO. IA and IB are **codominant**, so a person with both has blood group AB. This gene has **multiple alleles**, but each person inherits only two.

blocks.text: Most examples so far have had two alleles, one dominant and one recessive. Blood groups are different. This section covers the two new ideas.

items.meaning: A gene that has more than two alleles in a population. Each person still inherits only two.
Two alleles that are both expressed when they are present together. Neither is recessive.

items: A person's blood group is determined by their genotype.
One gene controls the ABO blood group. It has three alleles: **IA**, **IB** and **IO**.
Each person has two of these alleles, one from each parent.
IA and IB are codominant. IO is recessive to both of them.
Blood group is controlled by one gene with three alleles.
Each person has only two alleles, one from each parent.
IA and IB are codominant: both are expressed.

blocks.text: The genotype tells you the blood group. This section covers which genotypes give which group.

rows: IA is expressed. IO is recessive.
IB is expressed. IO is recessive.
IA and IB are codominant, so both are expressed.
No IA or IB is present, so the recessive allele shows.

items: To have blood group AB, a person inherits **IA** from one parent and **IB** from the other.
A person with blood group O must have inherited IO from both parents.
A person with blood group A or B can be homozygous or heterozygous.
AB is the only blood group where both alleles show.
Group O needs two copies of the recessive allele IO.
Groups A and B each have two possible genotypes.

sections.heading: Predicting the blood groups of children

blocks.text: Work out the children's blood groups the same way as any other cross. Pick the parents and see what is possible.

items.text: One parent is IA IO (group A) and the other is IB IO (group B).
The first parent makes IA or IO. The second makes IB or IO.
The children are IA IB, IA IO, IB IO and IO IO.
They are AB, A, B and O. Each has a 1 in 4 chance, so all four groups are possible.

diagram.alt: Pick two parents' genotypes and see the possible blood groups of their children.

options.label: IA IO × IB IO
results: IA IB, IA IO, IB IO, IO IO
options.explanation: Each parent passes on one of two alleles, so all four combinations are equally likely.

options.label: IA IA × IB IB
options.explanation: Every child inherits IA from one parent and IB from the other, so both alleles show.

options.label: IA IB × IO IO
options.explanation: The IO parent can only pass on IO. The children get either IA or IB from the other parent.

options.label: IA IB × IA IB
results: IA IA, IA IB, IA IB, IB IB
options.explanation: Two of the four boxes are IA IB, so AB is twice as likely as A or B.

options.label: IA IO × IA IO
results: IA IA, IA IO, IA IO, IO IO
options.explanation: IA is expressed whenever it is present, so three boxes in four are group A. Only IO IO is group O.

options.label: IA IB × IA IO
results: IA IA, IA IO, IA IB, IB IO
options.explanation: IA IA and IA IO are both group A, so A is the most likely.

options.label: IA IA × IO IO
options.explanation: Every child inherits IA and IO. IA is expressed and IO is recessive.

options.label: IO IO × IO IO
options.explanation: Neither parent has IA or IB, so no child can have group A, B or AB.

items: Use gametes and a Punnett square, as in any cross.
Two heterozygous parents with groups A and B can have children of all four groups.
Two group O parents can only have group O children.

checks.q: Describe how a person inherits the blood group AB.
checks.a: They inherit IA from one parent and IB from the other parent. The two alleles are codominant, so both are expressed.

checks.q: A person has the genotype IA IO. What is their blood group? Explain.
checks.a: Group A. IA is expressed and IO is recessive.

checks.q: What is meant by multiple alleles?
checks.a: A gene with more than two alleles in a population (such as IA, IB and IO), although each person inherits only two.

worked_example.question:
The blood group of a person is determined by their genotype.

Describe how a person inherits the blood group AB.
answer_points: They inherit A (IA) from one parent.
They inherit B (IB) from the other parent.
worked_example.tip: Any two of the three points score. It does not matter which parent gives which allele.

worked_example.question: Explain why the inheritance of blood group is an example of codominance.
answer_points: The alleles IA and IB are both present.
Both alleles contribute to the phenotype, as in blood group AB.

blocks.text: (Supplement) Blood groups are not the only example of codominance. Cattle show it in hair colour.

items: A red parent and a white parent can have roan offspring, with a mixture of red and white hairs.
Two roan parents give red, roan and white offspring in the ratio 1 : 2 : 1.
Both alleles contribute to the phenotype of a heterozygous animal.
